record.original_question: Let Ω be a round spherical disc of radius α < π/2 on the unit sphere S^2, and let Ω′ be a convex domain in S^2 with the same area as Ω. Show that there exists a bi-Lipschitz map from Ω′ to the Euclidean plane whose Lipschitz constants are 1 and α/sin(α), that is, a (1, α/sin(α))-bi-Lipschitz map.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Equip the unit sphere $S^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ with its standard round Riemannian metric, and let $d_{S^2}$ denote the induced geodesic distance. A subset $D \subset S^2$ is called a round (spherical) disc of radius $\alpha$ centered at $p \in S^2$ if $D = \{q \in S^2 : d_{S^2}(p,q) \le \alpha\}$. A subset of $S^2$ is called convex if for every two points in it there is a unique minimizing geodesic of $S^2$ joining them and this geodesic lies in the set.

Given constants $L_1, L_2 \ge 1$, a map $f : (X, d_X) \to (Y, d_Y)$ between metric spaces is called $(L_1, L_2)$-bi-Lipschitz if
$$\frac{1}{L_2}\, d_X(x,x') \;\le\; d_Y(f(x), f(x')) \;\le\; L_1\, d_X(x,x') \qquad \text{for all } x,x' \in X.$$

Fix $\alpha \in (0, \pi/2)$. Let $\Omega \subset S^2$ be a round spherical disc of radius $\alpha$, and let $\Omega' \subset S^2$ be any convex domain with $\operatorname{area}(\Omega') = \operatorname{area}(\Omega)$. Equip $\Omega'$ with the intrinsic metric inherited from $S^2$, and equip $\mathbb{R}^2$ with its Euclidean metric.

Prove that there exists a $\bigl(1, \tfrac{\alpha}{\sin \alpha}\bigr)$-bi-Lipschitz map $F : \Omega' \to \mathbb{R}^2$; that is, a map satisfying
$$\frac{\sin \alpha}{\alpha}\, d_{S^2}(x, y) \;\le\; \|F(x) - F(y)\|_{\mathbb{R}^2} \;\le\; d_{S^2}(x,y) \qquad \text{for all } x, y \in \Omega'.$$
